Szczuczyn Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Szczuczyn, Poland

Not demolished. Szczuczyn's Jewish population reached 2,506 people (56 percent of the town) by 1921. At the end of June 1941, a pogrom carried out by Poles killed several hundred Jews; a year later, the Germans killed most of the remaining Jewish population at Treblinka. This cemetery, likely established at the end of the 18th or beginning of the 19th century and certainly existing by 1845, was used as an execution and burial site for pogrom victims in 1941, with about 100 men murdered there on June 25 alone. A Communist-era monument in the cemetery, referencing the 1941 crime, bears an incorrect date; in 2016, researcher M. Tryczyk and priest W. Lemański gathered the few surviving damaged matzevot into one place.
